title: Plant
description: One plant record for the static plant database. Mirrors backend/app/models/plant.py and the create_plant_tables/add_taxonomy_climate_succession_fields_and_pest_interactions Alembic migrations: top-level fields map to the `plant` table, nested arrays/objects map to the satellite tables (plant_data_source, seed_info, plant_period, plant_companion, plant_bedding_need, plant_pest_interaction). See docs/schema.md for the full ER model. Every plant is one file: data/plants/<slug>.json.

slug.description: Primary key. URL-safe, unique, e.g. 'tomato', 'sweet-basil'. Must match the file's own name (<slug>.json).

sow_indoors.description: True if sowing_method explicitly says to start/sow seeds indoors. GitHub issue #177's investigation: never a derived false (absence of the word doesn't prove the opposite), and two other requested distinctions - a dedicated greenhouse flag, and 'direct-in-place' vs. 'direct-in-bed' as separate concepts - were investigated and dropped: 'greenhouse' appears in zero plants' sowing_method (the app already has bed-level Bed.has_greenhouse for that), and no source text actually distinguishes in-place from in-bed direct sowing as two different things.

sow_direct.description: True if sowing_method explicitly says 'direct seed'/'direct sow'. See sow_indoors' description for what this deliberately does NOT distinguish (in-place vs. in-bed) and why (GitHub issue #177).

needs_thinning.description: True if sowing_method or growing_information explicitly mentions thinning seedlings after they emerge. Never a derived false, same reasoning as sow_indoors/sow_direct (GitHub issue #177).

row_spacing_cm.description: Distance BETWEEN ROWS. Distinct from plant_spacing_cm (distance between individual plants within a row) - see backlog #170's investigation for why the two aren't the same number for many crops.

plant_spacing_cm.description: In-row spacing: distance between individual plants within the same row, as distinct from row_spacing_cm (distance between rows). GitHub issue #170's investigation found no structured source (openfarm, Trefle, Homesteader Labs, USDA PLANTS) distinguishes this from row spacing - each has exactly one generic spacing number, already mapped to row_spacing_cm. A genuinely distinct figure only shows up in a minority of plants' free-text growing_information/bedding_needs prose (old gardening books explicitly stating both 'rows X apart' and 'Y apart in the row'/'Y within the row') - populated there via manual-plant-spacing-derivation-tagged data_sources entries. Every other plant falls back to row_spacing_cm's value per the issue's own instruction (tagged manual-plant-spacing-fallback in data_sources) rather than being left null - callers should check the data_sources attribution if they need to know whether a value is genuinely independent or just a carried-over row_spacing_cm substitute.

growth_habit.description: Plant-shape category for the WYSIWYG bed editor's canvas rendering - what silhouette to draw, independent of height_cm/spread_cm (which give size, not shape). A small closed set designed for rendering, NOT a copy of Trefle's own raw growth_habit field (a free-text, comma-separated combination of USDA-style values like 'Vine, Forb/herb' - see data/CLAUDE.md's note on where that lives in Trefle's response and why it needed collapsing into something a renderer can switch on). Values: 'upright' = default clumping/branching growth, taller than wide, no vining/rosette/spreading tendency (most vegetables, upright herbs, alliums, grasses/corn) - drawn as a simple upright clump/oval. 'spreading' = low, wide, mounding, or ground-covering growth that spreads outward from its base without a trunk or climbing structure - covers both woody/subshrub bushes (currant, gooseberry, blueberry, sage, thyme, rosemary) and trailing/sprawling growth (strawberry runners, sweet potato, ground-grown winter squash) since both need 'wide, low canopy' rendering rather than 'tall and narrow' - drawn as a wide low canopy. 'climbing' = a vine that needs a trellis/support/fence to grow upward (peas, pole beans, cucumbers, grapes, hops, kiwi) - drawn along a support structure. 'rosette' = leaves radiate from a central point at/near ground level, often with the harvestable/storage part underground (root vegetables - carrot, beet, radish - and rosette-forming leafy greens - lettuce, spinach) - drawn as a flat low rosette, optionally with a root indicator below soil level. 'tree' = single-trunk woody tree with a canopy above ground level (the 2 real fruit trees, sour cherry and pear) - drawn tall with trunk + canopy. null = not confidently categorized (see growth_habit_unmatched.jsonl) - the frontend should fall back to a generic shape, not assume 'upright'.

water_needs_mm_per_week.description: Depth-rate, e.g. 25.4 for '~1 in/week'. Matches BedEquipment.water_delivery_lph's L/hour convention - later irrigation planning multiplies this by a bed's area to get an actual volume target (see docs/schema.md).

family.description: Taxonomic family, e.g. 'Solanaceae'. Used for rotation/succession-family logic.

genus.description: Taxonomic genus, e.g. 'Solanum'. Kept separate from botanical_name so rotation queries don't have to parse it back out.

parent_plant_slug.description: References another plant's slug (must resolve at import time, not enforceable in JSON Schema alone, and must not equal this plant's own slug) - the species/base plant this record is a named cultivar/variety of, e.g. 'brandywine-tomato'.parent_plant_slug = 'tomato'. Every cultivar stays its own full plant record (see data/etl/CLAUDE.md's cultivar-merge fix) - this is a hierarchy layered on top, not a merge. null = not (yet) confidently linked - either this plant isn't a cultivar of anything already in the database, or the link couldn't be determined without guessing (see data/etl/parent_plant_slug.py and data/parent_plant_slug_ambiguous.jsonl).

min_temperature_c.description: Natural habitat temperature range, not a US hardiness zone.

edible_parts.description: Closed list of edible-part categories (backlog #133), common-sense gardener groupings rather than strict botany - e.g. 'fruit' covers a strawberry even though it isn't one botanically. Values: 'fruit' (tomato, apple, squash, cucumber, pepper, berries in the everyday sense - the fleshy seed-bearing structure eaten as produce), 'leaves' (lettuce, spinach, kale, cabbage - cabbage's 'head' is a tight leaf cluster, not a flower structure), 'roots' (carrot, beet, radish - true roots), 'tubers' (potato, cassava - swollen underground stems/roots storing starch, kept distinct from 'roots' since a plant like cassava genuinely has both), 'bulbs' (onion, garlic, shallot - layered underground storage structures), 'stems' (celery, rhubarb, kohlrabi, cardoon's leaf-stalks, chard's midrib, leek's thickened stem base which is NOT a true bulb despite older sources sometimes calling it one), 'seeds' (sunflower, corn kernels, dry beans/peas eaten as the seed itself rather than in-pod), 'flowers' (broccoli and cauliflower's immature flower heads/curds, artichoke's flower bud, hops' cone - itself a cluster of flower bracts, courgette/squash blossoms, nasturtium), 'pods' (green beans, snap peas - eaten whole, pod and immature seed together, as opposed to 'seeds' which is the mature seed alone), 'shoots' (asparagus, sea kale, bamboo - a young stem/growth tip harvested before it matures into a stem proper). null/omitted = not populated (either genuinely not edible - see is_toxic/is_edible - or not yet categorized); an empty array is not used, omit the field instead.

succession_enabled.description: Whether this crop can be re-sown at intervals through the season rather than once.

life_cycle_years.description: A perennial's typical productive lifespan in years, e.g. 7 for raspberries (canes are perennial but a patch is usually renewed after ~7 years). Independent of life_cycle, not a 4th enum value - most perennials leave this null.

seed_info.description: Maps to the seed_info table (1:1 with plant). Omit entirely if nothing is known.

pretreatment.description: e.g. 'cold stratification 4 weeks', or null if none needed.

produces_viable_seeds.description: false for F1 hybrids and similar - null if unknown, not false.

periods.description: Maps to plant_period rows. Recurring annual windows (month only) - omit a period entirely rather than guessing start/end.

period_type.description: References a period_type.code row (e.g. 'sowing', 'planting', 'fertilizing', 'harvesting', or a later addition) - a lookup table, not a closed enum, so new period types don't need a schema change. Resolved/validated against that table at import time, not enforceable in JSON Schema alone.

companions.description: Maps to plant_companion rows. companion_slug must reference another plant's slug (resolved at import time, not enforceable in JSON Schema alone) and must not equal this plant's own slug.

mechanism.description: Open-ended, e.g. 'pest-deterrent', 'nitrogen-fixing', 'allelopathy' - why the relationship holds.

pest_interactions.description: Maps to plant_pest_interaction rows. Plant-to-insect relationships - distinct from companions, which is plant-to-plant.

pest_or_insect.description: e.g. 'aphids', 'ladybugs', 'tomato hornworm' - free text, not a closed enum.

need_type.description: Open-ended, e.g. ground_cover | hilling | staking - not a closed enum.

growing_information.description: Maps to plant_growing_information rows. Long-form growing-advice text (e.g. Project Gutenberg books with a section per plant) - deliberately unstructured, unlike every other field here. Intended to later be mined for the fields no structured source covers (composting_needs, fertilizer_needs, needs_wind_cover/needs_rain_cover, seed_info.pretreatment, bedding_needs - see data/CLAUDE.md's 'Fields still needing a source'), but that extraction isn't built yet - this just holds the raw material.

copyright_status.description: e.g. 'public domain', 'CC BY-SA 4.0', 'unknown' - free text, varies too much for a closed enum.

record_type.description: 'raw' = one source's excerpt as-is. 'consolidated' = synthesized from multiple raw entries for this plant. Defaults to 'raw' if omitted.

generic_for_species.description: true if this text was written about the species/genus generically (e.g. 'pumpkins') rather than this specific cultivar, and copied into every matching cultivar's record - not cultivar-specific advice.

data_sources.description: Maps to plant_data_source rows. Every non-trivial field elsewhere in this record should be traceable to at least one entry here - see data/CLAUDE.md's sources table for what's available to cite.
